facts.text: The post White House Bars CNN From Trump Flight a Day After Credentials Restored appeared first on TheWrap .
Then, on Monday, CNN, Politico and MS NOW sued President Trump and his administration after their reporters were stripped of their White House access and credentials.
"Without notice or process, the White House revoked our journalists' credentials because it objected to our reporting.
The decision to bar CNN from the flight was reportedly shared Friday evening in a note that laid out Trump's schedule.

Trump added: "There's something wrong with a country that can allow people to purposely tell negative stories … if they want to write them, that's fine, but I don't have to let them into my, into the people's house."

Anyway, let’s get into it… Trump Defends White House Ban On CNN, MS NOW and Politico, As Outlets Sue Over 1st Amendment Attack The most annoying thing about Trump’s constant attacks on the free press, including his recent banning of CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House, is that he is so obviously and demonstrably the “fake news” he has spent the last decade complaining about.
SEE ALSO: Surviving Trump: Trump Talks Boat Batteries And Sharks Again [Op-Ed] Trump Loses And Whines On Mail-In Voting, Kennedy Center, More [Op-Ed]

In the image, the only nation clearly shown is Greenland, which likely means this post was inspired by the new Greenland deal he’s been boasting about, even though it’s the same deal we have had with the nation for 75 years, with a few more bells and whistles. “I am pleased to announce that the United States of America has entered into an Agreement with The Kingdom of Denmark, and Greenland, that gives the United States permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland, completely addressing ALL of our many U.S. concerns,” Trump claimed in a lengthy social media post.
Since he announced the ban, Trump hasn’t once mentioned a specific grievance with any of the three outlets.
He also didn’t seem to understand that calling his current term “THREE” undermined the message he was going for.
The Trump White House is already trying to convince MAGA folk that an America First foreign policy means a war in distant Iran .
And now it’s attempting an even bigger stretch: convincing voters that their heavily touted mass-deportation push is no such thing.

White House Deputy Chief of Staff James Blair privately urged House Republicans on Tuesday to stop emphasizing “mass deportations” and instead focus their messaging on removing violent criminals, according to sources in the closed-door briefing …

But as Axios also notes, “mass deportation” in action polls poorly: “Nearly half — 49% — of Americans say Trump’s mass deportation campaign is too aggressive, including 1 in 5 voters who backed the president in 2024,” according to a Politico poll from January.
